data.title: Batman Appears Atop the Sydney Opera House for Batman Day 2026
data.description:
SYDNEY, AUSTRALIA / ACCESS Newswire / September 19, 2026 / As night fell over Sydney Harbour this Saturday evening, Batman appeared atop the sails of the Sydney Opera House to mark Batman Day 2026, striking his iconic pose and creating a spectacular sight as the Dark Knight was brought to one of Australia's most recognizable landmarks.

The larger-than-life moment formed part of DC and Warner Bros. Discovery's global Batman Day 2026 celebrations, which this year unites fans around the world under the theme "Rule the Night." The theme invites fans to see nightfall as a time for adventure, mystery and imagination, inspired by Batman protecting Gotham City after dark.

Batman Day is celebrated on the third Saturday of September each year, with Batman's striking appearance on the Sydney Opera House forming part of a global celebration of the Dark Knight. Throughout September, fans around the world are coming together for Batman Day events across the U.S., Europe, Asia and Latin America.

data.title: Starbucks's Snoopy cups and McDonald's SpongeBob toys are commanding huge markups on eBay
data.description:
By Bill Peters

Adults are scooping up promotional items out of nostalgia - and playing into a frenzy around collectibles

Starbucks launched its "Peanuts"-themed fall collection on Tuesday.

Customers this week snapped up limited-time gear from Starbucks's "Peanuts" fall collection and McDonald's new "SpongeBob SquarePants" toys - and now they're being resold online for a premium.

After Starbucks (SBUX) launched its collection of glass Snoopy cold cups and other gear featuring Charlie Brown and Linus on Tuesday, the items had largely sold out on its website. The Snoopy cup was going for as much as $120 on Etsy (ETSY), compared with the $40 price listed on Starbucks's website.

As for the McDonald's (MCD) "SpongeBob" Happy Meal toy line that also launched on Tuesday, some eBay (EBAY) merchants were selling the entire set of those toys for around $90. And a set of "Dragon Ball Super" figurines launched by Burger King (QSR) this month, along with cups and a paper crown, was selling for more than $40.

Of course, other merchants were selling those items for lower prices or had recently slashed their prices, and prices can be negotiated downward. But the demand and price swings have arrived amid a booming market for collectibles, with people increasingly treating items like trading cards and toys as investments.

Neil Saunders, a retail analyst at GlobalData, said the toys and other gear offered by restaurants particularly appeal to that market given that they often arrive in the form of limited drops. Other factors also add a sense of scarcity.

"You have to be a member of a particular tier in a loyalty scheme or make a particular purchase to get them," he said. "Because of that, it makes them desirable and interesting. And of course, once it goes on an auction site like eBay, it's very easy for that price to go up."

Happy Meals and other toy promos were geared toward children in the past. But Saunders noted that they're now more likely to be geared toward adults, who might be lured by nostalgia or the collectibles frenzy. Additionally, social media has made it easier for items to go viral, and brands have become more savvy about what might resonate with consumers.

A Starbucks spokesperson told MarketWatch the company increasingly sees its ancillary offerings - like cups and other gear - as collectibles. The company declined to offer sales figures on the "Peanuts" items or details on the exact percentage of stores selling them, nor did it say whether it had seen any unusual buying activity surrounding the items.

McDonald's did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Neither did Burger King parent Restaurant Brands International.

The Starbucks items featuring the "Peanuts" characters - known for animated classics like "It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown" - were intended to promote the return of Starbucks's pumpkin-spice latte. The move follows the coffee chain's other recent collaborations with Hello Kitty, the clothing and accessories brand Roller Rabbit and the fashion brand Dandy. Those efforts have been part of the company's turnaround plan, which has shown signs recently of taking hold.

Earlier this year, limited-edition Imax (IMAX) popcorn buckets, designed to look like the Imax camera Christopher Nolan used to film "The Odyssey," began popping up on eBay at inflated prices.

Saunders also noted that a Dunkin' promo this year offering a free tote bag with the purchase of a half-dozen doughnuts went over well with customers. And he called out the enduring appeal of Trader Joe's tote bags.

"They've become super popular, to the extent that they've been popping up in Japan and the U.K., where there are no Trader Joe's," he said. "Why are people interested in this basic tote bag? I think it's because it just becomes a viral sensation online, and it becomes a real collectible thing, and it becomes a must-have item."

-Bill Peters

data.title: I just started dating someone I really like, but he's moving to Mexico for six months. Should I spend the money to visit him?
data.description:
By Aditi Shrikant

'Traveling is something we both want in a partnership'

"I want to be smart about how much I spend on such a new relationship."

Dear Dollar Signs,

I met a guy two months ago and I really like him. He told me he is not seeing other people, and neither am I. Every year he goes to Mexico for six months. It really helps his mental health and is an important part of his life. He is doing it again this year and wants me to visit him. We live in Denver.

Should I spend the money and PTO to feel like I'm keeping this relationship afloat, or does it create a false sense of excitement? I don't feel like there's some mile marker we should hit first, especially being more financially rounded in my mid-30s, but I want to be smart about how much I spend on such a new relationship.

Traveling is something we both want in a partnership. If the relationship grows, we would have to learn how to set money aside to keep that as a priority.

Smitten and Spending

If you're just starting out on your money or career journey and have questions about how to navigate your finances, we want to hear from you. Write to Dollar Signs, MarketWatch's new advice column, at dollarsigns@marketwatch.com.

Dear Smitten,

Oh, I'm so jealous! The first two months of a relationship, when you realize the feelings are not only mutual but growing, is such a special time.

I personally think it's a green flag that he isn't willing to change a long-standing tradition for someone he met so recently. In my experience, when a person molds their life to please a potential partner early in the courtship, it can mean they don't have a strong sense of self. His dedication to spending time in Mexico, while inconvenient for your relationship, demonstrates that he knows how to manage and nurture his own happiness and isn't relying on you to satisfy that need.

Budgeting for this trip is not dissimilar from budgeting for any other vacation. Spend within your means. After paying your non-negotiable costs like rent and bills, contributing to your retirement and emergency savings accounts, and paying down debt, how much do you have left? This is the maximum amount you should be spending, no matter who you're flying to see. No one is worth taking on debt or neglecting long-term financial goals for.

The real question is whether or not you want to be in a long-distance relationship, says Lisa Marie Bobby, a relationship therapist.

Six months is a lot of time. And while long-distance relationships can foster a distinct type of intimacy because of how much conversation and communication is needed to sustain them, they also can (famously) lead to delusion.

"The hard part of a long-distance relationship is there is a component of fantasy that could creep in that clouds understanding of the relationship or what is going on," Bobby says. "If you are not with someone a whole lot in real life, there can be information about them you miss - energetically, observationally."

You will be spending limited time with him in person, which means you'll be filling in a lot of blanks yourself. Two months in, the rose-colored lenses are especially obfuscating. In the absence of information, you'll likely choose the most flattering answer.

I'd talk to him about whether he is willing to fly back to Denver to see you during this time, if only to alleviate some of the financial burden. Planes fly both directions. His answer will indicate the amount of effort he plans to put in.

You also need to be honest with yourself about what you want your future to look like. If you like traveling and see yourself eventually being able to live in Mexico part-time, that is important information. However, if Denver is where you want to be most of the year, I'm not sure this relationship will work in the long term.

I'm also curious about your dating history. Do you tend to hop from one relationship to another, or is liking someone this much really rare for you? If you think he is different from other people you've gone out with, putting in a bit more time and money to get to know him might be worth it.

The excitement of a burgeoning relationship is often fueled by a lack of information. That is OK. The point of traveling to see him is to learn more about each other and see whether this thing has legs. As long as you aren't going into debt to figure that out, I think this could be a lovely arrangement.

Write to Dollar Signs at dollarsigns@marketwatch.com.

By submitting your story to Dow Jones & Co., the publisher of MarketWatch, you understand and agree that we may use your story, or versions of it, in all media and platforms.

-Aditi Shrikant

data.title: Stocks face a growing list of threats - so why are investors staying so calm?
data.description:
By Isabel Wang

Investors are well aware of the risks, but they have simply decided none are significant enough to force them out of the market

Stocks have every reason to sell off, but they refuse to budge

On the surface, this looks like the easiest quarter stocks have had in years.

The S&P 500 is up modestly in recent months and moving in a narrow lane, while the Cboe Volatility Index - known as Wall Street's "fear gauge" - is snoozing near its lowest level of the year. That's despite the Iran war pushing oil prices above $100 a barrel, a new Federal Reserve's interest-rate hike and artificial-intelligence executives publicly begging their own industry to slow down.

The stock market's reaction to all of it? A shrug.

All three major indexes on the U.S. stock market have been churning sideways in the third quarter of 2026 - with the S&P 500 SPX up 2% through Friday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA off 1.2% and the Nasdaq Composite COMP up 1.2% in the period, according to FactSet data. More notably, despite all the macroeconomic and geopolitical drama, the S&P 500 has not seen a 2% daily move in either direction since June 5.

Even the options market, which is inherently more aggressive and forward-looking than the equity market, isn't panicking either. The Cboe Volatility Index VIX closed Friday at 14.81, just above its 2026 closing low of 14.25, hit on Aug. 14. A VIX reading below 20 is seen as signaling a calm, stable stock market where investors expect low volatility over the next 30 days.

"The 'Spider-Man' market is again climbing 'a wall of worry,'" Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, told MarketWatch on Friday. "Investors are not ready to give up on stocks. They are willing to take some trading profits occasionally when markets rally, but they're not really willing to part with their favorite shares even though they are seeing some erosion."

The erosion isn't visible from the surface, but the broader market is facing a growing list of risks.

First, the Federal Reserve has just begun a new monetary-tightening cycle, delivering its first rate hike in more than three years earlier this week. Oil prices (CL00) (CL.1) (BRN00) above $100 a barrel, driven by the Iran war, also remain front and center, pushing gasoline prices across the country above an average of $4.47 a gallon and squeezing consumer budgets. Meanwhile, recent calls from industry leaders to slow the development of advanced AI have triggered a temporary plunge in global chip stocks DRAM.

Looming in the background are rising long-term Treasury yields, with the benchmark 10-year rate BX:TMUBMUSD10Y having climbed above what many view as the critical 5% level. Higher yields make borrowing more expensive for consumers and businesses, putting pressure on stock valuations and increasing the cost of government debt.

To be sure, any one of these headlines could, on its own, be enough to move the stock market significantly. Instead, stocks have spent the past three months locked in a relatively narrow trading range. Market analysts say investors are well aware of the risks in front of them; they have simply decided, at least for now, that none are significant enough to force them out of the market.

"The market is now saying, 'I don't know,'" said Mike Treacy, head of risk at Apex Fintech Solutions. "On one hand, you have a very healthy growing economy. On the other hand, that economy is being financed by the AI build-out, and then interest rates are going higher, so it causes you to pause to the upside."

Mark Hackett, chief market strategist at Nationwide's Investment Management Group, said neither bulls nor bears have been able to "gain a clear advantage" since May, with inflation and rate uncertainty balanced against continued strong earnings growth.

"The Fed's first rate hike in three years confirmed that inflation, not growth, is again the central policy risk, and the lack of equity-market reaction suggests investors agree with that path and it was well communicated," Hackett said in emailed commentary.

Robust corporate earnings so far this year have indeed provided the fundamental support for major indexes to trade in record territory. This profit engine has helped absorb significant macro headwinds and keep equity valuations anchored.

"Investors have decided that earnings are what matter, and earnings do matter," said Sosnick at Interactive Brokers. "That's why the upside in stocks eventually hinges upon stocks' ability to deliver on increasingly rosy earnings expectations - not just for the next quarter or two, but for the quarters to come."

But some are still hedging their bets rather than rushing for the exits. Apex's Treacy pointed to a significant decrease in speculative trading in September, with the notional trading volume in U.S.-listed leveraged ETFs projected to reach just $24 billion this month, down from nearly $52 billion in June, according to data compiled by Apex.

"The tape has changed in that there is less speculation than there was in the first half of the year - and that puts us in 'Nowheresville,' where you have a healthy economy [and] a healthy job market, but also interest rates at extreme levels and oil at elevated levels," Treacy told MarketWatch in a phone interview on Friday.

U.S. stocks closed Friday mostly lower for the week. The Dow was off 1.7% on the week, while the S&P 500 fell 0.1% and the Nasdaq gained 0.7%, according to FactSet.

-Isabel Wang

Fast Guard Service Expands Nationwide Emergency Fire Watch Response for Businesses and Properties

Fast Guard Service Expands Nationwide Emergency Fire Watch Response for Businesses and Properties

PR Newswire

HOLLYWOOD, Fla., Sept. 19, 2026

Security provider strengthens rapid-response fire watch coverage for commercial properties, construction sites, hotels, residential communities and facilities requiring immediate life-safety monitoring.

HOLLYWOOD, Fla., Sept. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fast Guard Service, a nationwide security and fire watch provider, announces the continued expansion of its emergency fire watch response program, providing businesses and property managers access to trained personnel when fire protection systems are impaired or additional fire monitoring is required.

Fast Guard Service provides 24/7 fire watch coverage across the United States, including emergency and last-minute deployments. The company's nationwide operating model is designed to mobilize personnel rapidly, with a goal of arriving at many emergency assignments within four hours of deployment.

Fire watch personnel conduct scheduled patrols of designated areas, monitor for signs of fire or hazardous conditions, maintain required fire watch logs and follow site-specific post orders. Services are available for properties experiencing sprinkler or fire alarm impairments, construction activity, system maintenance and other circumstances requiring dedicated fire monitoring.

"When a fire protection system goes down, property owners and managers may need qualified personnel quickly," said Roderick C. Payne Jr., President of Fast Guard Service. "Our objective is to make obtaining emergency fire watch coverage as straightforward as possible while providing clients with communication and documentation throughout the assignment."

Fast Guard Service supports commercial buildings, hotels, condominiums, apartment communities, construction projects, retail properties, warehouses, healthcare facilities and other locations requiring temporary or ongoing fire watch coverage.

Clients can request service,receive a quote and coordinate deployment through Fast Guard Service's nationwide operations team.

Founded in 2013, Fast Guard Service provides armed and unarmed security, fire watch, event security, executive protection, construction security, patrol services and emergency security response throughout the United States. The company operates 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

data.title: AI leaders want to 'pace the frontier' as part of a safety slowdown. But how?
data.description:
By Christine Ji

Tech giants are attempting to put aside their rivalries and unite on AI safety, but they're clashing over how an actual slowdown would work

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, at right, has proposed slowing the rate of AI development while introducing new regulatory protocols. OpenAI's Sam Altman and SpaceX's Elon Musk agree.

Artificial-intelligence leaders rarely agree on anything.

As Anthropic, OpenAI, Alphabet's (GOOGL) (GOOG) Google and other AI labs compete in an expensive race to develop superintelligence, they've diverged on everything from open-source access to model architecture. It's led to fierce disputes that sometimes veer into name-calling.

So when Elon Musk, Sam Altman and Demis Hassabis - the heads of xAI parent SpaceX (SPCX), OpenAI and Google DeepMind - expressed support for Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's calls to slow the development of AI, it seemed like the tech executives had put aside their differences to tackle serious technological risks. They agreed that the "frontier," an industry term for the most state-of-the-art AI capabilities, is progressing at a rate faster than humans can safely monitor and control.

Concerns about powerful AI systems causing societal harm through cyberattacks and economic disruption have flared after AI researcher Jacob Coxon announced his resignation from Anthropic earlier this month, saying in an X post that OpenAI and Anthropic are acting irresponsibly and "gambling with our lives." Anthropic's head of alignment science, Evan Hubinger, echoed that sentiment, posting on X that he sees a "greater than 10% chance" of AI eliminating humanity within the decade.

Amodei's essay "We Must Pace the Frontier" addressed those concerns by urging the AI industry to build new capabilities at a slower rate. More resources must be dedicated to model alignment, or ensuring that an AI model's behaviors match human values and intentions, he argued. Amodei also called for increased regulation of the frontier AI labs, with a focus on "transparency and third-party auditing."

But implementing guardrails for safe AI development is turning out to be far more complicated than simply voicing support on social media. New heated debates are flaring up across the industry as CEOs, researchers and policymakers grapple with what it means to pace the frontier.

First, not everyone agrees that AI safety is a collective-action problem.

The frontier labs have embraced working together to set standards. OpenAI global policy chief Chris Lehane said on Tuesday that the company had been collaborating on AI safety issues with Anthropic and Google DeepMind for several weeks.

OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind did not immediately respond to MarketWatch requests for comment.

On the other hand, Meta (META) CEO Mark Zuckerberg took a different stance, saying in a Tuesday X post that "every lab has the responsibility and incentive to move at the pace required to train its models safely, and the ability to take its own actions to ensure that happens." Zuckerberg highlighted that Meta delayed the release of its Muse AI agent for several months due to safety reasons. "We didn't call for everyone else to do this before we would," he added.

Meta did not immediately respond to a MarketWatch request for comment.

Ritwik Gupta, a computer science and AI professor at the University of Maryland, believes that pacing the frontier is contingent upon on widespread cooperation among labs. "That may not be possible in today's competitive free-market regime that we operate in," Gupta said. If only OpenAI and Anthropic agree to slow AI development, other players could seize the opportunity to catch up or set a new frontier, he pointed out.

Even if AI labs collaborate to slow development, Gupta sees potential for loopholes to emerge. Some researchers have proposed limitations on the computing power used to train AI. Today's frontier progress is increasingly driven by test-time workloads and software development surrounding AI rather than just raw model training, according to Gupta.

"I'm not fully convinced that pausing training alone is actually going to meaningfully change the rate of progress of the frontier," Gupta said.

The lack of shared definitions across a fast-moving industry is also stalling AI safety efforts.

A.J. Bhadelia, who oversees Americas public policy at Cohere, told MarketWatch that there remains "fundamental scientific disagreement in that space." In his opinion, some of the recent discussions about AI risk have approached the territory of "science fiction."

"That 10% number is not based on research...there's no scientific validity to that," Bhadelia said of the Anthropic researcher's doomsday prediction.

The AI industry needs to have an evidence-based discussion about the types and severity of AI risks before rushing to impose policies, he argued, as a consumer-facing AI tool could require a very different set of guardrails than an enterprise infrastructure provider.

While pacing the frontier sounds compelling in theory, some believe these ambiguous definitions and loopholes make a slowdown functionally impossible.

"In practice, there is no coherent, rational slowdown plan to be considered," Ben Goertzel, the founder of SingularityNET, said. A prominent AI researcher, Goertzel and DeepMind co-founder Shane Legg popularized the term "artificial general intelligence" in the early 2000s. As AI applications proliferate, Goertzel raised the question: "Where do you draw the line between AI development and software development?"

"There's a premise underlying all of this that you can control AI by controlling the biggest LLMs," Goertzel told MarketWatch.

Goertzel pointed to startups such as Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs, founded by Meta's former chief AI scientist Yann LeCun, and Discovery Loop, launched by ex-Google DeepMind chief scientist Jeff Dean. These companies are exploring experimental architectures that could challenge the industry's current training practices.

"I think the assumption that only a few companies can be at the frontier may not look so true a year from now," Goertzel said. "The smaller the cutting-edge things get, the harder it is to police."

One proposal that has picked up widespread traction is the use of independent evaluators within labs. In his essay, Amodei proposed placing "embedded evaluators" within frontier labs and giving these auditors employee-level access to monitor AI practices.

But again, the initial consensus gives way to a barrage of new questions. Who should do the auditing? Who will govern the auditors? And what types of evaluations should be administered?

Zuckerberg took a laissez-faire approach, writing in his Tuesday post that Meta Superintelligence Labs already engages independent evaluators and "other labs can just do this too."

A non-profit organization called Model Evaluation and Threat Research has grown in prominence recently after being mentioned in Amodei's essay as a potential third-party evaluator. But University of Maryland professor Gupta believes federally funded research and development centers (FFRDCs) would serve as more neutral third-party evaluators.

FFRDCs are government-funded, privately operated research centers that include private, non-profit think tanks and major research universities. The incentive structure for a congressionally funded FFRDC is less vague than philanthropy-backed AI safety groups, Gupta said.

On Friday, a group of independent AI evaluation organizations called the AI Evaluator Forum published a public letter outlining a general framework for embedded evaluators. With over 100 signatories, the letter called for diversity in evaluations and operational safeguards to help evaluators maintain independence.

"The independence question is very important," Nat Purser, director of U.S. policy at the AI Verification and Evaluation Research Institute, told MarketWatch. The institute is a signatory of the AI Evaluator Forum letter.

"People are right to think about conflicts of interest and not being involved in commercial entanglements with the labs," Purser said. Over the past few weeks she's received questions about whether auditors can speak freely without retaliation from the labs and if evaluators can gain sufficient access to the necessary materials needed to conduct an audit.

"A lot of this is going to have to be effectuated through policy if we want to see this standardized across the labs," Purser added. One proposal to promote evaluator independence would be for regulators to assign auditors from a licensed pool instead of having the labs hire their own auditors directly.

However, Purser cautioned that setting up an effective evaluator system won't be sufficient to catch all AI threats, as unforeseen risks will inevitably emerge.

"I'm not interested in pacing for pacing's sake," Purser said. "I'm more interested in implementing more processes that allow for meaningful oversight, and if that results in things slowing down, that'd be great."

-Christine Ji

data.title: Chery Auto to Showcase Nearly 20 Green Technology and Ecosystem Innovations. 2026 Chery International User Summit Opens in October
data.description:
Chery Auto to Showcase Nearly 20 Green Technology and Ecosystem Innovations. 2026 Chery International User Summit Opens in October

Chery Auto to Showcase Nearly 20 Green Technology and Ecosystem Innovations. 2026 Chery International User Summit Opens in October

PR Newswire

WUHU, China, Sept. 19, 2026

WUHU, China, Sept. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Chery Auto will host the 2026 Chery International User Summit from October 18 to 24 at its global headquarters in Wuhu, China. Focused on technology, sustainability and convergence, the Summit will showcase nearly 20 green technologies and ecosystem innovations, highlighting Chery Auto's progress toward becoming a global high-tech green ecosystem enterprise.

The Summit will bring together users and ecosystem partners to explore intelligent, low-carbon mobility and sustainable lifestyles.

From January to August 2026, Chery Group sold 725,214 new energy vehicles (NEVs), up 46.2% year on year. Chery Auto's hybrid engine has achieved a thermal efficiency of 48.57%, while the company is advancing all-solid-state battery technology with an energy density of 400 Wh/kg.

Chery Auto is also reducing carbon emissions across the vehicle lifecycle, from R&D and manufacturing to use and recycling. Through vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology, smart charging, battery recycling and material reuse, it is developing a circular system spanning energy production, storage, use and recycling, positioning NEVs as nodes in smart energy networks.

More than 3,000 AiMOGA embodied AI humanoid robots, developed by Chery Auto, have been delivered in more than 60 countries and regions, covering over 100 use cases across smart manufacturing, commercial services and the home.

At the Summit, Chery Auto will feature AI-powered cockpits, future mobility, human-machine collaboration and other applications integrating smart technology with green energy. Further technologies will be unveiled at the event.

Chery Auto works with international organizations including the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) on nature conservation, education and community initiatives. The Summit will also feature Ride Green Life, a global charity ride bringing users and ecosystem partners together to promote low-carbon living.

Chery Auto's products and services have reached more than 130 countries and regions, serving millions of owners worldwide. From October 18 to 24, users, the media and ecosystem partners will gather in Wuhu for technology demonstrations, green initiatives and owner activities, exchanging ideas on green mobility, smart technology and sustainable living. The Summit will showcase Chery Auto's transformation from automaker to "creator of better lives" and its vision for a smarter, lower-carbon and more sustainable future.

data.title: GAC Cambodia KD Plant Starts Production, Setting a New Benchmark for Localized Manufacturing
data.description:
GAC Cambodia KD Plant Starts Production, Setting a New Benchmark for Localized Manufacturing

GAC Cambodia KD Plant Starts Production, Setting a New Benchmark for Localized Manufacturing

PR Newswire

KAMPONG CHHNANG, Cambodia, Sept. 19, 2026

KAMPONG CHHNANG, Cambodia, Sept. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On September 17, the inauguration ceremony of GAC Cambodia KD Plant was grandly held in Kampong Chhnang Province. Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet and Chinese Ambassador to Cambodia Wang Wenbin attended the ceremony, while Jiang Xiuyun, Deputy General Manager of GAC Group, and Wang Shunsheng, Deputy General Manager of GAC International and President of the Southeast Asia Regional Center, together with the leadership of TH Group, GAC's strategic partner in Cambodia, witnessed the official launch of the THAM assembly plant for GAC vehicles. This marks a new stage in GAC's development in Cambodia, transitioning from complete vehicle exports to local manufacturing, and stands as yet another achievement of China-Cambodia economic and trade cooperation.

Prime Minister Hun Manet was present in person to witness this important moment. He noted that the official commencement of the GAC KD Plant is a significant achievement of the Royal Government of Cambodia's industrial transformation, helping Cambodia upgrade from labor-intensive industries to capital-, advanced-technology- and high-skill-driven sectors, spurring local industrial development, raising the added value of the national economy, and cultivating new sources of economic growth.

From complete vehicle imports to local assembly, GAC has steadily built its presence in Cambodia. The project was fully launched in 2024, and through close collaboration among all parties, the plant completed all preparatory and construction work and officially entered production. Under this local assembly project, TH Group is responsible for plant investment, construction and vehicle assembly, while GAC supplies complete knocked-down (CKD) kits, technical standards and full-chain technical support. With a designed annual capacity of around 10,000 units.

Strong market performance further validates the results of GAC's deep cultivation. TRUMPCHI has enjoyed explosive growth in Cambodia since 2024, with an average annual compound growth rate of over 300% over the past three years, and ranked first among Chinese automotive brands in Cambodia in 2025, with continuously expanding brand influence.

The production launch of GAC Cambodia KD Plant marks a brand-new starting point for GAC's deep cultivation in Cambodia. Over the past seven years, from channel development to product rollout, from brand establishment to manufacturing upgrading, GAC has been sharing development opportunities with the Cambodian people through tangible capacity, employment and technology.

For further information about GAC, please visit: https://www.gacgroup.com/en or follow us on social media.

data.title: Best Sunglasses for Every Face Shape (2026): Quay Named Top Pick for Wide Faces, Low Nose Bridges, and Larger Heads by Expert Consumers
data.description:
Best Sunglasses for Every Face Shape (2026): Quay Named Top Pick for Wide Faces, Low Nose Bridges, and Larger Heads by Expert Consumers

Best Sunglasses for Every Face Shape (2026): Quay Named Top Pick for Wide Faces, Low Nose Bridges, and Larger Heads by Expert Consumers

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Sept. 19, 2026

NEW YORK, Sept. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Expert Consumers has named Quay the top pick for wide faces, low nose bridges, and larger heads in a new guide to the best sunglasses for every face shape. The 2026 review highlights Nightfall Extra Large, Say Less, and Good Time as examples of how frame width, bridge construction, and silhouette can address different fit concerns.

Best Sunglasses for Every Face Shape

  • Quay - offers sunglasses in multiple sizes, shapes, bridge constructions, and lens options for a wide variety of faces.

Face shape and physical fit require separate consideration. Frame shape influences visual balance, while measurements determine whether sunglasses remain comfortable and properly positioned. Even a flattering silhouette can pinch at the temples or slide down the nose when the frame dimensions do not suit the wearer.

The guide recommends starting with shape before reviewing width, bridge design, arm length, and lens coverage. This process helps narrow the selection without treating traditional face-shape guidance as a rigid rule.

Face Shape and Frame Fit Require Separate Consideration

Finding suitable sunglasses begins with two questions: which silhouette balances the face, and which measurements fit comfortably? Expert Consumers recommends using face shape to narrow the visual options before checking frame width, bridge design, arm length, and lens coverage. Both stages affect the final result.

Round faces commonly suit square, rectangular, and cat-eye frames because angular lines add definition against softer contours. Square faces can benefit from rounded lenses that balance a stronger jawline. Oval faces accommodate many silhouettes, including aviators, while heart-shaped faces often pair well with cat-eye frames that direct attention toward the cheekbones.

Face-shape guidance remains a starting point rather than a strict rule. A frame should meet the face comfortably at the temples, remain level across the brow, and provide sufficient eye coverage. Arms that bow outward may indicate inadequate width, while repeated sliding can signal an unsuitable bridge.

Lens protection also remains essential. Frame shape and fit may guide the aesthetic decision, but verified UV protection addresses the primary functional purpose of sunglasses.

Wider Frames Provide More Room at the Temples

Sunglasses for wide faces should provide enough horizontal space to avoid excessive temple pressure. Wider measurements can create a more natural fit, while deeper lenses may help the frame remain visually proportional. Quay's Nightfall Extra Large applies these dimensions to a shield silhouette.

Nightfall Extra Large measures 151 mm across, with a 19 mm bridge, 145 mm arms, and a 52 mm lens height. The width provides more room than many standard sunglasses, making the frame a practical option for broader faces.

A one-piece lens creates substantial coverage without a thick surrounding rim. The flat upper line gives the oversized design a structured appearance, while built-in universal nose pads provide a straightforward bridge fit.

No frame width guarantees comfort across every facial structure. Temple position, bridge placement, frame material, and arm curvature also influence pressure. Nightfall Extra Large provides a useful starting point for shoppers who regularly find standard sunglasses too tight at the sides.

Low-Bridge Frames Help Reduce Sliding

Low-bridge sunglasses are designed for faces where standard frames sit too low, slide forward, or make contact with high cheekbones. Adjustable nose pads can improve bridge contact and raise the lenses, helping the frame remain better positioned without relying on a fixed molded bridge.

Say Less combines adjustable silicone nose pads with a 147 mm aviator frame. A 16 mm bridge and 53 mm lens height give the style generous coverage while allowing the bridge position to be refined.

The frame pairs pressed metal temples with an acetate Windsor rim. This construction gives the aviator more visual weight than a conventional wire frame without making the adjustable fit details conspicuous.

The silicone pads can be positioned to support a lower bridge and create more clearance above high cheekbones. Fit still depends on individual nose and cheek contours, making virtual try-on or an in-person fitting useful before purchase.

Say Less demonstrates that low-bridge construction can appear across familiar fashion silhouettes. Adjustable support does not require a purely functional appearance or a limited range of frame shapes.

Angular Sunglasses Balance Round Faces and Larger Heads

Round faces often benefit from frames with straight lines and defined corners. For larger faces, both the overall frame width and lens width are important, along with how the arms sit at the temples. Quay's Good Time combines a geometric rectangular profile with enough horizontal width to avoid the proportions of a petite frame.

Good Time measures 145 mm across, with a 19 mm bridge, 145 mm arms, and a 34 mm lens height. The low-profile rectangle introduces angles that contrast the softer curves of a round face.

Tall temples and beveled frame detailing add structure at the sides. The slim lens height creates a clean horizontal effect, while the overall frame width provides more room than many small or narrow-fit sunglasses.

The product description uses "narrow rectangle" to identify the lens silhouette rather than an especially narrow overall frame. This distinction allows Good Time to provide a sleek appearance while retaining a 145 mm total width.

Correct fit should allow the arms to extend backward without pronounced outward flaring. The frame should sit near the temples without excessive pressure or overhang. These checks remain necessary even when the angular silhouette appears balanced from the front.

Expert Consumers selected Quay for the range of options across extended sizing, adjustable bridge construction, and face-shape categories. Nightfall Extra Large addresses width and coverage, Say Less supports lower bridges through adjustable nose pads, and Good Time combines angular styling with broader proportions.

Frame measurements should be reviewed before purchase because facial width, bridge height, and temple position vary. Quay's size filters and virtual try-on feature may help narrow the available options before an in-person fitting.

The full review is available at Expert Consumers.

About Quay

Quay is a global eyewear brand offering a wide selection of sunglasses and prescription glasses. The company's collections emphasize contemporary design, functional lens features, and pricing that remains accessible to a broad range of consumers. Quay products are available through its direct-to-consumer website, Quay stores and select retail partners worldwide.
